title: Cycle times on three molding machines
intro:
The cycle time (s) of ten parts was recorded on each of three injection-molding machines. Machine 3 sometimes stalls. Check the assumptions before comparing the machines, and run the rank-based test that does not need normality.

Find Levene's W (median-centered) and its p-value, the Kruskal–Wallis H and its p-value, and Welch's F and its p-value. Give W, H and F to two decimals and the p-values to three decimals or more.

To use the Workbench: press **Copy the data**, press Ctrl+B, click **+ Data table** and paste (Ctrl+V). Choose **One-way ANOVA** in the list on the left, set **Data table** to the table you pasted, **Layout** to *Each column is a group*, leave **Group columns** blank (every column) and set **Significance level (α)** to 0.05. Ctrl+L brings you back.

Levene.says: That is Levene's original test, with distances from each group's mean. Statistics+, like scipy's stats.levene and R's car::leveneTest, centers on the median: zᵢⱼ = |yᵢⱼ − median of group i|, then a one-way ANOVA on the z's.
That is Bartlett's statistic. Levene's W is the F of a one-way ANOVA on the distances from the group medians.

KruskalH.says: That is the ANOVA's F. Kruskal–Wallis ranks all 30 values together and compares the groups' mean ranks.

WelchF.says: That is the ANOVA's F, which pools the three variances into one MS within. Welch's F weights each group by nᵢ/sᵢ², so Machine 3's large spread does not swamp the other two. Read it under Kruskal–Wallis in the Workbench.

WelchP.says: That is the ANOVA's p-value, from the pooled F. Welch's p uses Welch's F and its own denominator df (about 16 here, not 27).

hints: Levene: for each value, its distance from its own group's median. Then run a one-way ANOVA on those distances; W is its F.
Levene's p is the area above W under the F curve with k − 1 = 2 and N − k = 27 df: Python stats.f.sf(W, 2, 27), R pf(W, 2, 27, lower.tail = FALSE).
Kruskal–Wallis: rank all 30 values (1 = smallest, ties share the average rank); H = 12/(N(N + 1)) × Σ Rᵢ²/nᵢ − 3(N + 1), with Rᵢ the rank sum of group i. Compare H with χ² on k − 1 = 2 df.
Welch's ANOVA: the Workbench gives Welch F, Welch denominator df and Welch p-value at the bottom of the results. R: oneway.test(y ~ g, var.equal = FALSE).
